why: Both moved the same five call sites behind the one AsyncOpenAI client with the same honest list of what stays (Bedrock, Azure, the VMind subprocess), but A shipped more of Router's actual surface in the migration itself — spend label, per-call-site prompt cache key, provider_timeout, model map, then built cross-vendor fallbacks and Flex — and backed it with the only real measured economics in either report ($0.000501 → $0.0000423 on a repeated agent-step prefix) plus the discovery that the documented per-role [llm.*] sections were dead code. B's execution is cleaner (all six branches pass the outside check, better-designed per-agent labels, careful BYOK exclusions in the model map, and rigorous negative results), but A's system-level reading of this product — capability lookup restoring the browser agent's eyes, model choice per role made real, history compaction plus Switchyard named as the top proposal against the dominant cost of resending the whole conversation each step — is the deeper one.
A_best: Router leverage actually exercised and measured: policy-level cache keys/labels/provider_timeout in the migration, fallbacks and Flex built, a live -92% cost measurement on a realistic agent step, and the find that per-role [llm.*] config had never taken effect, which is the plumbing every later model-choice decision needs.
B_best: Disciplined correctness and product-specific judgment: per-agent spend labels via a contextvar (right granularity for an app where every call comes from app/llm.py), a model map that deliberately refuses BYOK Gemini/Bedrock ids, the planning-flow fixes (tool_choice REQUIRED on the one call the whole run derives from, None guard, right-sized summary), and two measured non-changes — including not trimming duplicate prompts because it would break the cache prefix.
A_worst: Four of six improvement branches fail the outside check's parse gate on a syntax error A introduced in data_visualization.py, unmentioned in the report; and its per-role label scheme collapses to "default.*" for every agent until an operator writes config sections, which A's own live data shows.
B_worst: Less Router surface actually used — fallbacks, provider_timeout and tier are left as proposals because router.policy.json was unavailable, cost claims lean on the fact sheet rather than its own measurement, and the calls table wrongly attributes the vision paths to [llm.vision], the very per-role resolution that does not work.
